bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Climate change and GHG emissions (energy management) — BRSR flags climate change mitigation and energy management as risks with negative financial implications - GHG emissions from the business contribute to global warming, and continued reliance on non-renewable energy leads to higher CO2 emissions and environmental damage. Mitigation is a focus on renewables under a detailed Decarbonisation roadmap.
- Hazardous and non-hazardous waste management — Improper disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous waste leads to significant regulatory, environmental and social issues and may impose reputational and financial risk; mitigated by recycling and co-processing to reduce waste going to landfill.
- Water use and availability — Water is a shared resource between communities and the business; responsible consumption, recycling and reuse are essential, addressed through a strategy aimed at minimising the overall water footprint. Flagged with negative financial implications.
- Regulatory compliance across a multi-country footprint — Non-compliance leads to legal penalties and litigation and reduces trust and brand reputation; the Company relies on regular and periodic reviews of current and upcoming compliance requirements. Relevant given operations and registrations across many jurisdictions.
- Process safety and occupational health & safety — Process safety concerns prevention of unintentional chemical releases or accidents during manufacturing that could harm people, property or the environment. Most Indian sites are ISO 45001:2018 certified, with additional ISO certifications being considered for all UPL sites.
- Counterfeit products — Counterfeit product can harm customers and the brand; addressed via supply chain controls, inspections and advanced authentication technologies to protect product integrity and consumer safety.
- Export and geographic concentration — Exports contribute 65.15% of total turnover of the entity, so earnings are structurally exposed to overseas demand, trade dynamics and currency movement - the Board's Report attributes part of FY26 revenue growth to favourable foreign exchange movements.
- Sector cyclicality - commodity prices and farm economics — The MD&A describes a preceding macro-period of turbulent global commodity prices and widespread farm economics stress, and a challenging macroeconomic environment impacting the global agricultural sector; the business remains exposed to input/output price cycles, mitigated through high-value innovation and product differentiation that de-risk it from legacy commodity price volatility.
- Business-activity concentration in chemicals — Manufacturing of chemical and chemical products accounts for 83.20% of standalone turnover (with wholesale trading at 16.80%), concentrating the standalone entity in a single, heavily regulated product category.
- Execution risk on pending corporate restructuring — The proposed Advanta IPO and the Composite Scheme of Arrangement consolidating India and international crop protection into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited are subject to requisite statutory and regulatory approvals, so the intended simplification and value unlocking are not yet certain.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report does not disclose a capex programme, project-wise outlay or dated commissioning schedule. Expansion is described as footprint and utilisation rather than new capacity: an end-to-end backward integrated manufacturing ecosystem spanning 43 state-of-the-art global facilities that optimises asset utilisation, ensures supply assurance and maintains proximity to customers while mitigating input cost volatility, with a global presence across more than 140 countries covering manufacturing facilities, field stations, R&D chemistry centres, new Agtech/NPP sites, Global Capability Centres and Advanta in-house and R&D facilities in geographies including the USA, Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Costa Rica, Colombia, Indonesia, India, South Korea, China, the UK, France, Italy, Mauritius, Israel, Ukraine, Hungary, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Australia, Spain, Belgium, Vietnam, Thailand and South Africa. During FY26 the Company established and scaled up three state-of-the-art Global Capability Centres in India, Colombia and Mauritius, consolidating global functions across finance, supply chain, human resources and marketing; these three centres are now fully operational. Capacity growth came from higher utilisation rather than new lines - EBITDA growth was supported by improved contribution margins on account of enhanced capacity utilisation and lower input costs, with the resilient global supply chain optimising capacity utilisation across the manufacturing base alongside inventory optimisation and input cost management. Portfolio/geographic expansion was inorganic and structural rather than greenfield: DECCO was successfully integrated with Advanta, capturing synergies, widening the portfolio and strengthening regional channels; Advanta expanded its global seed franchise and SUPERFORM strengthened its presence in specialty chemicals, with super specialty chemicals expanding across paints, mining, rubber, nutraceuticals and pharmaceuticals. Two structural corporate actions are pending: the proposed IPO of Advanta Enterprises Limited (DRHP filed with SEBI and the Stock Exchanges in January 2026, in-principle approval received on March 12, 2026), and a Composite Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Board on February 20, 2026 to consolidate the India and International Crop Protection businesses into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited, which is proposed to be independently listed, subject to requisite statutory and regulatory approvals.

business_model.title: What they do

The business is run through pure-play platforms: UPL Corporation Ltd. (global crop protection), UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions Ltd. (India crop protection), Advanta (seeds and post-harvest, including DECCO) and SUPERFORM Chemistries Limited (specialty chemicals).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Agriculture at an inflection point - climate volatility, resource constraints, geopolitical shifts, labour shortages and growing food-security need are reshaping the global agricultural landscape and raising urgency for productivity-enhancing innovation
- Industry cycle recovery: post-COVID destocking, falling active-ingredient prices and channel dynamics drove a correction lasting nearly 18 months; conditions began to stabilise by end-2024 with further improvement in FY26
- Volume-led growth and strong customer demand, with recovery across North America and Europe and stable momentum in LATAM and Rest of World
- Margin levers: richer/differentiated product mix, supply-chain discipline, improved capacity utilisation, lower raw material costs, portfolio rationalisation and structural process efficiencies
- Rising innovation rate - share of revenue from products launched within the past five years increased from 14% in FY25 to 16% in FY26
- Increasing demand for sustainable agriculture driving the NPP (biologicals, biocontrols, biostimulants) platform, addressing soil health, crop resilience and reduced reliance on synthetic inputs
- Nutrient-use efficiency identified as a significant opportunity, with technologies that reduce fertiliser requirements deployed across Brazil, Argentina and India
- Increasing demand for high-quality seeds supporting Advanta's expansion across new geographies and crop segments
- Diversified portfolio across platforms and geographies reduces concentration risk and cushions market volatility
- Watch items entering FY27: evolving geopolitical and supply-chain challenges, evolving trade dynamics and subdued commodity prices pressuring farm economics
- Regulatory/registration capability as a driver - over 2,500 dossiers submitted and around 2,700 approvals secured during the year
- Crop protection pipeline valued at approximately $4.4 billion at peak sales potential, of which around $1.5 billion is expected to be realised by FY30; nearly 80% of the pipeline comprises differentiated and sustainable solutions
- 27 molecules in active development and 17 solution platforms advancing through the pipeline
- NPP / sustainable solutions pipeline includes 10 new technologies at various stages of development
- Key R&D programme cyproflanilide advanced during the year and is expected to become a meaningful contributor in the years ahead
- More than 300 new products launched globally in FY26, generating over $160 million in revenue

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report does not disclose a capex programme, project-wise outlay or dated commissioning schedule. Expansion is described as footprint and utilisation rather than new capacity: an end-to-end backward integrated manufacturing ecosystem spanning 43 state-of-the-art global facilities that optimises asset utilisation, ensures supply assurance and maintains proximity to customers while mitigating input cost volatility, with a global presence across more than 140 countries covering manufacturing facilities, field stations, R&D chemistry centres, new Agtech/NPP sites, Global Capability Centres and Advanta in-house and R&D facilities in geographies including the USA, Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Costa Rica, Colombia, Indonesia, India, South Korea, China, the UK, France, Italy, Mauritius, Israel, Ukraine, Hungary, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Australia, Spain, Belgium, Vietnam, Thailand and South Africa. During FY26 the Company established and scaled up three state-of-the-art Global Capability Centres in India, Colombia and Mauritius, consolidating global functions across finance, supply chain, human resources and marketing; these three centres are now fully operational. Capacity growth came from higher utilisation rather than new lines - EBITDA growth was supported by improved contribution margins on account of enhanced capacity utilisation and lower input costs, with the resilient global supply chain optimising capacity utilisation across the manufacturing base alongside inventory optimisation and input cost management. Portfolio/geographic expansion was inorganic and structural rather than greenfield: DECCO was successfully integrated with Advanta, capturing synergies, widening the portfolio and strengthening regional channels; Advanta expanded its global seed franchise and SUPERFORM strengthened its presence in specialty chemicals, with super specialty chemicals expanding across paints, mining, rubber, nutraceuticals and pharmaceuticals. Two structural corporate actions are pending: the proposed IPO of Advanta Enterprises Limited (DRHP filed with SEBI and the Stock Exchanges in January 2026, in-principle approval received on March 12, 2026), and a Composite Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Board on February 20, 2026 to consolidate the India and International Crop Protection businesses into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited, which is proposed to be independently listed, subject to requisite statutory and regulatory approvals.

themes.title: Agrochemicals & crop-input cycle recovery
themes.need: Crop-protection is recovering off a brutal trough, and Q1FY27 shows domestic branded volume decoupling from generic exports. RALLIS grew revenue only 7% yet lifted EBITDA 23% to a ~18.0% margin (+230bps) as domestic B2C rose 19% on +15% volume while exports COLLAPSED 28% (volume -35%) on Chinese pricing, and its seeds EBITDA margin went 26% to 30% on a rice/maize/millet mix versus price-controlled cotton - though PAT +31% is flattered by an INR 35cr employee-provision reversal of which INR 24cr is genuinely one-time, so normalise before extrapolating. The monsoon is the live variable: as of 8-Jul seasonal rainfall was ~15% below normal with kharif acreage ~21% below last year. SUMICHEM delivered record FY26 profitability; INSECTICID/DHANUKA/SHARDACROP ride premiumization + technicals; COROMANDEL/GNFC/CHAMBLFERT/GODREJAGRO add fertilizers + integrated agri.
themes.driver: Monsoon catch-up and kharif acreage recovery from ~21% below last year; domestic B2C volume against continued Chinese export price pressure; new molecule launches and biologicals scale-up.
